_metadata.artifact_kind_note: Hand-authored seed artifact produced by scripts/05_extract_reverts.sh against the local clone. Unlike most other data artifacts, this one is fully derivable from the local git history with no network access required — it consumes only git log --grep against the default branch and (when reverts exist) git merge-base --is-ancestor against the release-tag inventory in data/releases.json. The reverts[], exclusions.*[], and summary.reverts_by_release_tag{} fields are populated as empty because the three independent revert-detection searches documented in search_commands[] each return zero matches against this clone at the documented extraction_timestamp. When the script is re-run, the values will reflect that execution; on this repository they are expected to remain zero unless an explicit Revert commit is pushed to main.
_metadata.confidence_rationale: Revert detection is a direct local-git scan with no API, network, or admin-access dependency. The three search patterns in search_commands[] are AAP-canonical (§0.5.3.9) and all three return zero on this clone. There is no intermediating system that could mask the signal; an empty result here is High-confidence evidence of zero reverts, not a degraded fallback.

exclusions.unattributable_note: Empty because zero revert commits were found; an entry would appear here only when a revert commit's original SHA could not be resolved via either (a) explicit 'Reverts commit <SHA>' reference in the revert message body or (b) tree-match against a prior commit whose tree equals the revert's parent tree. The detection logic for these conditions is implemented in scripts/05_extract_reverts.sh and is dormant on this repository because the upstream revert search produced no candidates.
exclusions.unreleased_note: Empty because zero revert commits were found; an entry would appear here only when an attributable revert's original commit is not reachable from any release tag (i.e., git merge-base --is-ancestor returns non-zero for every tag in data/releases.json#releases). Doubly empty for this repository because data/releases.json#summary.total_releases is also zero (verified by `git tag -l | wc -l` returning 0).
exclusions.revert_of_revert_note: Empty because zero revert commits were found; an entry would appear here only when a revert's original commit subject itself begins with 'Revert' (i.e., the revert is undoing a previous revert). Per AAP §0.5.3.9 these are excluded from the attributable count as confidence indicators rather than counted as net new problem records.

summary.reverts_by_release_tag_note: Object (not array) so that release tags become keys when the array is non-empty; the empty object signals 'no reverts attributed to any release' rather than 'release dimension not yet computed'. Cross-references data/releases.json#summary.total_releases which is 0 for this repository.
summary.ramp_up_steady_state_split_reason: Per data/inflection.json#phase_decomposition.ramp_up_steady_state_split_reason — post-introduction span (86 days) is shorter than 90 days; AAP §0.5.3 mandates baseline/post-introduction-only reporting. Both phase values are zero on this repository.

search_commands_note: Both AAP-canonical commands from §0.5.3.9 are listed here for the Reproducibility Appendix (Rule 5). The first command scans across all refs (refs/heads/, refs/remotes/, refs/tags/) with the strict subject prefix 'Revert "' (the convention emitted by `git revert <SHA>` without --no-edit) and produces the per-commit metadata needed for resolution if any match is found. The second command scans only the default branch with a slightly relaxed prefix 'Revert ' (no embedded double-quote required) and serves as a counting/verification command. Both must return zero match-bodies on this repository.

search_verification.tertiary_corroboration_note: An additional cross-validation against the standard 'This reverts commit <SHA>' body line emitted by `git revert` (regardless of subject-line edits). Zero matches across all refs confirms the absence of reverts independently of subject-line prefix conventions.
search_verification.broadest_corroboration_note: Case-insensitive scan of all commit subjects across all refs for any line starting with 'Revert' after the 40-char SHA. Zero matches confirms no commit subject (across all branches, remotes, and tags) begins with the word 'Revert' in any casing.
search_verification.verification_summary: All four independent search variants — primary AAP command, secondary verification command, body-text corroboration, and broadest subject scan — return zero matches against the clone at HEAD 3fe40fa33e31da4985007b1b7e7b7dd7842f0fdb on branch blitzy-721d7d10-a0c0-47d3-b010-cfb636cb8bd8. This is High-confidence evidence of zero reverts in the repository's commit graph.

extraction_logic.step_1_enumerate_revert_candidates: git log --all --grep='^Revert "' --pretty=format:'%H|%aI|%aE|%s|%B%n----' is parsed into per-commit records. Each record carries the revert commit SHA, author ISO timestamp, author email, subject line, and full body. With zero candidates on this repository, this step produces no records and Step 2 is skipped.
extraction_logic.step_2_resolve_original_sha_per_candidat: For each candidate, the revert body is searched for an explicit 'This reverts commit <40-char-SHA>' reference (the convention emitted by `git revert`). If absent, a tree-match is attempted: find the prior commit whose tree object equals the candidate's parent tree. Failure to resolve in either path emits an unattributable exclusion entry. Skipped on this repository because zero candidates.
extraction_logic.step_3_attribute_to_release: For each resolved original SHA, iterate the release-tag inventory in data/releases.json#releases (most recent first) and find the most recent tag T where `git merge-base --is-ancestor T <original-SHA>` returns exit code 0. The candidate revert is then attributed to release T; if no tag in the inventory is an ancestor, an unreleased exclusion entry is emitted. Skipped on this repository because Steps 1 and 2 produce no records.
extraction_logic.step_4_filter_revert_of_revert: For each attributed revert, check whether the original commit's subject begins with 'Revert' — if so, emit a revert_of_revert exclusion entry. Skipped on this repository because no attributable reverts exist.
extraction_logic.step_5_aggregate: Group attributable reverts by attributed_release_tag into summary.reverts_by_release_tag and aggregate counts. On this repository the result is the empty object {}.

boundary_conditions.zero_reverts_in_period: Zero reverts on main in the analysis period 2026-02-23 → 2026-05-21. Verified by all four search variants above and consistent with the absence of any 'Revert' subject across the full 538-commit roster (data/commits.csv).
boundary_conditions.zero_release_tags: Per data/releases.json, this fork has zero annotated release tags. Even if a revert existed, the attribution step would emit an 'unreleased' exclusion for any revert whose original commit is not reachable from a tag. The combination 'zero reverts + zero tags' is the empty intersection — no signal to report for m8 attribution, but the metric value (count of revert commits) is still 0 by direct count, which is High confidence.
boundary_conditions.metric_value_independent_of_release_inve: The Metric 8 value reported in metrics.json#m8.value is the count of attributable revert commits, which is 0 here. It does not depend on the release inventory being non-empty — a revert that cannot be attributed to a release becomes an unreleased exclusion (also 0 here) rather than a denominator gap. The High confidence is preserved by the fact that the numerator measurement (revert detection) is a direct, complete local-git operation.

provenance.spec_definition_excerpt: Count of revert commits on the default branch attributed to the release that contained the original (reverted) commit. For each revert: (a) identify the original commit being reverted via the 'Reverts commit SHA' reference in the revert message, or by tree-match against a prior commit's parent if no explicit reference is present; (b) identify the most recent release tag T such that T is an ancestor of the original commit; (c) attribute the revert to release T.
exclusion_categories_per_spec: unattributable — revert's original commit cannot be identified
unreleased — revert's original commit not reachable from any release tag
revert_of_revert — the original is itself a revert

cross_artifact_consistency.expected_companion_artifact_revert_candi: data/revert_candidates.csv must contain only the header row (commit_sha|author_date|subject) with no data rows; verified by `wc -l blitzy/acceleration-report/data/revert_candidates.csv` returning 2 (header + trailing newline).
cross_artifact_consistency.verification_command: python3 -c "import json; r=json.load(open('blitzy/acceleration-report/data/reverts.json')); m=json.load(open('blitzy/acceleration-report/data/metrics.json')); assert r['summary']['attributable_reverts'] == 0 and r['summary']['total_revert_commits_found'] == 0 and m['m8']['value'] == 0 and m['m8']['confidence'] == 'high'"
cross_artifact_consistency.rule_4_internal_consistency_guarantee: The single numeric value 0 reported in metrics.json#m8.value MUST equal summary.attributable_reverts in this artifact. The renderer reads only metrics.json; the compute step reads only this artifact (and data/releases.json for the attribution dimension). Any drift between the two would fail the make-verify spot-check.
